display.purpose: The product value of a roll, in Lucky Gold. The largest and heaviest type in the system.

numeral.purpose: The three die faces, in the same gold, one step below the product they make.

headline.purpose: The wordmark, filled with a 135 degree Iris-to-Gold gradient clipped to the text.

verdict.purpose: The won/lost pill. The multiply and equals operators share the size at 600 in Fog.

title.purpose: Card headings. Small enough that a card reads as a panel rather than a page section.

body.purpose: The default, and the input value size, so a typed stake matches the surrounding text exactly.

cell.purpose: Table cells, the player name, and the value inside a quick pick at 600.

label.purpose: Field labels and the odds legend. Sentence case, not uppercased.

label-caps.purpose: Table column headers, uppercased and tracked. Quick stakes, badges and field errors share the size without the uppercasing.

caption.purpose: The prediction echo under the product, and the row labels the history table grows on mobile.

micro.purpose: The probability and payout line inside a quick pick. The floor; nothing goes smaller.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: On every card, always identical. Separates the surface from the ground without implying hierarchy.

shadows.name: action-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary button hover only, paired with a 1px lift. The only colored shadow in the system.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Atmosphere on a focused input at 1.23:1. Never the indicator; the 2px Iris Text outline is.

shadows.name: shadow-float
shadows.purpose: The toast, the one genuinely floating element, slightly heavier than a card.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Every pointer response: hover, focus, border and background shifts, the 1px lift.

motion.name: roll
motion.purpose: Die tiles on every result. Full 360 degree Y rotation with the scale dipping to 0.8 at the halfway point; dice, product, prediction caption and verdict all land together at 200ms, mid-flip.

motion.name: balance-mark
motion.purpose: The balance marking direction: Teal with a 1.1 scale on a credit, a 0.97 settle on a debit.

motion.name: toast-slide
motion.purpose: Toast entering from 100px below and leaving the same way after an 8 second hold or a dismiss.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion the flip, the lifts and the balance scale are dropped while the dice still change, the balance still marks direction in colour, and the toast still arrives on opacity.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The roll action. Full width, one per card, the only element that visibly rises off the surface.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 100%; padding: 0.75rem 2rem; border: none; border-radius: 8px; background: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); color: #fff; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s, transform 0.2s, box-shadow 0.2s; } .ds-btn-primary:hover:not(:disabled) { background: var(--primary-hover, #7f70f0); transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: 0 4px 12px rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.4); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary-text, #8f83f4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Quick Pick
components.description: A predicted product with its real win probability and payout, both counted at runtime from the 216 ordered rolls. Shown at rest, selected, and in the best-return variant. 12 and 24 tie exactly, so best is a pair.
components.css: .ds-picks { display: flex; gap: 0.4rem; flex-wrap: wrap; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-pick { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; min-width: 62px; padding: 0.4rem 0.7rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); font-family: inherit; line-height: 1.2; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s, background-color 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-pick-value { font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-pick-meta { font-size: 0.7rem; font-weight: 400; color: var(--text-on-tint, #a8acc0); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-pick:hover { border-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); background: var(--surface-hover, #22263a); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-pick:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary-text, #8f83f4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-pick[aria-pressed="true"] { border-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); background: rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.2); color: #fff; } .ds-pick--best { border-color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); background: rgba(255, 211, 42, 0.08); } .ds-pick--best:hover, .ds-pick--best[aria-pressed="true"] { border-color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); background: rgba(255, 211, 42, 0.2); }

components.name: Quick Stake
components.description: Adds a fixed amount to the stake field rather than setting it, so two taps build $260. Teal because it puts money on the table.
components.css: .ds-stakes { display: flex; gap: 0.4rem; } .ds-stake { padding: 0.35rem 0.7rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 6px; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); color: var(--success, #00b894); font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; cursor: pointer; transition: border-color 0.2s, background-color 0.2s, transform 0.2s; } .ds-stake:hover { border-color: var(--success, #00b894); background: rgba(0, 184, 148, 0.1); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-stake:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary-text, #8f83f4); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Filled with the page ground so the control reads as punched into the card. The constraint rides in the label, and errors answer beneath the field rather than in a toast.
components.html: Three dice cannot make 13. Try 12 or 15.
components.css: .ds-field { font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-field__label { display: block; margin-bottom: 0.3rem; font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); } .ds-field__note { color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); font-weight: 400; } .ds-field__input { width: 100%; padding: 0.7rem 1rem; border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 8px; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); font-family: inherit; font-size: 1rem; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: border-color 0.2s; } .ds-field__input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(108, 92, 231, 0.2); } .ds-field__input:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary-text, #8f83f4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-field__input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--danger, #e17055); } .ds-field__error { margin-top: 0.35rem; font-size: 0.8rem; color: var(--danger-text, #e8846b); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The only container in the system. Every card carries the same border and the same ambient shadow, whatever it holds.
components.html:
Place Your Bet

Cards stack in one 900px column with a 1.5rem gap.
components.css: .ds-card { background: var(--surface, #1a1d27); border: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 12px; padding: 1.5rem; box-shadow: 0 4px 24px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.3); font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); } .ds-card__title { margin: 0 0 1rem; font-size: 1.1rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-card__body { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); }

components.name: Dice Equation
components.description: The signature component, never hidden. It rests at ? x ? x ? = ? from first paint and carries the prediction under the product, so the comparison has both sides. Hover the row to replay the roll.
components.html:

components.css: .ds-equation { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.7rem; flex-wrap: wrap; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-die { width: 64px; height: 64px; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: var(--bg, #0f1117); border: 2px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); border-radius: 12px; font-size: 1.8rem; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-equation:hover .ds-die { animation: ds-roll 0.4s ease-in-out; } @keyframes ds-roll { 0% { transform: rotateY(0deg) scale(1); } 50% { transform: rotateY(180deg) scale(0.8); } 100% { transform: rotateY(360deg) scale(1); } } .ds-op { font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); } .ds-product-group { display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; min-width: 84px; } .ds-product { font-size: 2rem; font-weight: 800; line-height: 1.2; color: var(--accent, #ffd32a); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-product-caption { font-size: 0.75rem; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-product-caption.ds-matched { color: var(--success, #00b894); font-weight: 600; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-equation:hover .ds-die { animation: none; } }

components.name: Balance Pill
components.description: The player's money, in the header. It marks which way the balance moved: Teal and a 1.1 scale on a credit, a 0.97 settle on a debit. Hover to see the credit state.
components.css: .ds-identity { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-identity__name { font-size: 0.9rem; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); } .ds-balance { min-width: 110px; padding: 0.4rem 1rem; border-radius: 20px; background: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); color: #fff; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 700; text-align: center; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; transition: transform 0.2s, background-color 0.2s; } .ds-identity:hover .ds-balance { transform: scale(1.1); background: var(--success, #00b894); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-identity:hover .ds-balance { transform: none; } }

components.name: Outcome Badge
components.description: The won/lost and credit/debit pair. Full-strength text on a 15% tint of its own colour, never a solid fill. The loss variant uses Clay Text, since full Clay only reaches 4.35:1 on its own tint.
components.html: WONLOSTWON
components.css: .ds-badges { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 1rem; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-badge { display: inline-block; padding: 0.15rem 0.6rem; border-radius: 12px; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 600; } .ds-badge--won { background: rgba(0, 184, 148, 0.15); color: var(--success, #00b894); } .ds-badge--lost { background: rgba(225, 112, 85, 0.15); color: var(--danger-text, #e8846b); } .ds-status { padding: 0.3rem 1.2rem; border-radius: 20px; font-size: 1.3rem; font-weight: 700; } .ds-status--won { background: rgba(0, 184, 148, 0.15); color: var(--success, #00b894); border: 1px solid var(--success, #00b894); }

components.name: History Tabs
components.description: Local navigation inside the history card. A real tab pattern: roving tabindex, aria-selected, arrow keys, one tab stop for the group.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border, #2a2e3e); font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; } .ds-tab { padding: 0.7rem 1.5rem; border: none; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; background: none; color: var(--text-muted, #8b8fa3); font-family: inherit; font-size: 0.95rem; font-weight: 500; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.2s, border-color 0.2s; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--text, #e4e6eb); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--primary-text, #8f83f4); outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-tab[aria-selected="true"] { color: var(--primary-text, #8f83f4); border-bottom-color: var(--primary, #6c5ce7); }

components.name: Error Toast
components.description: Server and network failures only; validation answers at the field. Carries role=alert, a dismiss control and an 8 second hold rather than a 3 second expiry.
components.html: The bet could not be placed. Check your connection and try again.
components.css: .ds-toast { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.75rem; max-width: 30rem; background: var(--danger, #e17055); color: #fff; padding: 0.8rem 0.8rem 0.8rem 1.5rem; border-radius: 8px; font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9rem; font-weight: 500; box-shadow: 0 4px 20px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4); } .ds-toast-dismiss { flex: none; width: 28px; height: 28px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; background: none; color: #fff; font-family: inherit; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1; cursor: pointer; opacity: 0.75; transition: opacity 0.2s; } .ds-toast-dismiss:hover { opacity: 1; } .ds-toast-dismiss:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #fff; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
The room is dark and the instruments are on. Surfaces are Midnight Slate and its two lighter siblings, hairline borders separate everything, and the type is the operating system's own UI face at rest. Then three dice land in Lucky Gold and the terminal admits, briefly, that it is a casino. That contrast is the whole system: a composed readout that keeps one warm light burning over the table.

It is precise and composed first. Values are exact, the rhythm repeats, controls answer in two tenths of a second with a single pixel of lift, and nothing is approximate. But it is not solemn. The wordmark carries a drawn die, the dice rest at ? x ? x ? = ? before you have bet anything, and the quick picks tell you your real chance of winning and what it pays before you spend a cent. The system knows it is a dice game and is willing to say so, as long as it says so in the same measured voice it uses for the ledger. The wit is in the arithmetic, not in borrowed glyphs: no emoji stands in for an icon, and no star stands in for a number.

Depth is tonal, never dramatic. The palette is disciplined about meaning: violet is the only color that acts, gold is the only color that rolls, and teal and clay only ever report an outcome. Confirmed rejections: this system does not become neon slot-machine chrome (gradient bevels, glow spam, confetti, coin shine), and it does not become a crypto trading terminal (tickers, sparklines, wall-to-wall red and green, manufactured urgency).
keyCharacteristics: One 900px column of stacked cards on a Midnight Slate ground, with a single width breakpoint at 600px and one input breakpoint at pointer: coarse.
A three-step tonal ramp does all structural depth work; the one card shadow is atmosphere.
Controls are punched into the card, not raised off it. Only the primary action rises.
Gold has exactly four homes: three in the game, one in the identity that quotes it.
Zero font requests. Zero image requests. The only artwork is one drawn 5-pip die, used as both favicon and mark.
Every state change is 0.2s, with a 1px lift and a colored glow on the primary action.
The equation is never hidden. It rests at ? x ? x ? = ? and carries the prediction under the product, so the comparison always has both sides.
Every number the interface states about odds is counted at runtime, never transcribed.

rules.name: The Iris Means Action Rule
rules.body: Violet marks what the visitor can do and who they are. If an element is not actionable, not focused, and not the balance, it does not get Iris.

rules.name: The Gold Only Rolls Rule
rules.body: Lucky Gold has four homes and no more: the numerals of a roll, the product they make, the picks marked best, and the far end of the wordmark gradient. The first three are the game itself; the fourth is the identity quoting it. Adding a fifth costs the rest their meaning.

rules.name: The Outcome Pair Rule
rules.body: Teal and Clay report results and nothing else. They never become brand colors, never decorate, and never appear on an element whose meaning is not won/lost or credit/debit.

rules.name: The Zero-Request Type Rule
rules.body: The system loads no font files. Type costs nothing at first paint today, and a webfont is a trade to argue for rather than a default to reach for.

rules.name: The Weight Before Size Rule
rules.body: Emphasis is bought with weight (600, 700, 800) before it is bought with size. Only the roll result is allowed to be both.

rules.name: The Single Column Rule
rules.body: Everything below the header is one column of cards at one measure. The bet row is the only place the system nests a grid, and it collapses at the single breakpoint.

rules.name: The Tone Ramp Rule
rules.body: Structural depth comes from Midnight, Surface and Raised. Shadow never ranks importance and never gets heavier to make something matter more.

rules.name: The Inset Control Rule
rules.body: Anything that accepts input recedes to Midnight Slate with a Slate Line border. Only the primary action rises off the surface, and it rises in Iris.

rules.name: The Shared Corner Rule
rules.body: Cards and dice both take 12px, so a rolled die reads as a small card rather than a foreign object dropped into the layout.

rules.name: The Pill Means Status Rule
rules.body: The 20px pill is reserved for things that report a live value: the balance and the won/lost verdict. Actions never wear it.

rules.name: The Two-Tenths Rule
rules.body: Every state change runs 0.2s. Only events are allowed longer: the roll at 0.4s, the toast at 0.3s, the balance mark at 400ms. If it responds to a pointer, it is 0.2s.

rules.name: The One Loud Thing Rule
rules.body: Each card gets at most one element at full saturation: the Iris button in the bet card, the Gold product in the result card, the badges in the history. Everything else in that card is neutral. The odds legend is the standing test: it sits above the button in neutral badges precisely because a second solid-Iris element in that card read as a second submit.

rules.name: The Nothing Precedes The Dice Rule
rules.body: No part of an outcome may appear before the dice that produce it. The verdict, the winnings, the matched caption and the balance all wait for the same frame. A result on screen always belongs to the bet the visitor is currently looking at, or the card is showing ?.

rules.name: The Numbers Are Counted Rule
rules.body: Any probability, payout or count the interface states is derived at runtime from the 216 ordered rolls, never transcribed into markup. Four of the eight quick picks once carried hand-written percentages and four of them were wrong, one by a factor of two. A number the code cannot recompute is a number the interface is not entitled to claim.

rules.name: The Direction Is The Feedback Rule
rules.body: The balance marks which way it moved: Teal and a 1.1 scale on a credit, a 0.97 settle on a debit. One gesture for both is a celebration attached to a loss.

dos: Do keep Lucky Gold on the game. Its four homes are the die numerals, the product, the best-odds picks, and the far end of the wordmark gradient.
Do recess controls into Midnight Slate with a 1px Slate Line border, and let only the primary action rise.
Do answer every pointer in 0.2s with a 1px lift. Crisp, with a spring in it.
Do hold the 900px single column and let the one 600px breakpoint collapse the bet row and shrink the dice.
Do reserve Teal and Clay for won/lost and credit/debit, always as a 15% tint under full-strength text.
Do pair every quick pick with its real win probability and payout, both counted at runtime. Telling the visitor their odds is part of the voice; telling them wrongly is worse than silence.
Do keep type on the system stack unless a webfont earns the request it costs.
Do answer validation at the field that caused it, and keep the toast for failures the client cannot predict.
Do give every focusable element the same Iris Text outline at 2px with a 2px offset.
Do announce the outcome of a roll in the live region: rolled, product, predicted, paid, new balance.
Do set every comparable number in tabular figures, right-aligned in tables.
Do state a field's constraint in its label, before the visitor can break it.
donts: Don't drift into neon slot-machine chrome: no gradient bevels, glow spam, confetti, sparkles, or coin shine on the gold.
Don't drift into a crypto trading terminal: no tickers, no sparklines, no wall-to-wall red and green numerals, no manufactured urgency.
Don't rank importance with shadow. Every card carries the same ambient shadow; depth is tonal.
Don't give Iris a second job. It means action, focus and identity, never decoration.
Don't put two full-saturation elements in one card.
Don't introduce a second colored shadow. The Iris action glow is the only one.
Don't use the 20px pill for anything actionable; it belongs to live values.
Don't write a probability, payout or count into markup by hand. Count it.
Don't show any part of a result before the dice land, or leave a previous result on screen during a roll.
Don't let a table push the document sideways. Wrap it, or collapse it to records.
Don't identify a row by its position in the list. Use the id the service returned.
Don't put a raw API field name in front of a visitor.

Don't kill motion wholesale under prefers-reduced-motion. Remove the movement, keep the state change: the dice still turn over, the balance still marks its direction in colour, the toast still arrives.
